parts.problem_md:
This question is about two organic compounds, **X **and **Y.** Both are liquids which contain carbon, hydrogen and oxygen only.

The mass of hydrogen and of carbon present in 1.33 g of **X** were determined by passing its combustion products through the apparatus shown.

![q2a-paper-3-jan-2022-edexcel-ial-chemistry](assets/023-q2a-paper-3-jan-2022-edexcel-ial-chemistry.png)

i) State the** measurements** that should be made.

**(2)**

ii) Give **two** reasons why pure O<sub>2 </sub>(g), and **not** air, should be used.

**(2)**

iii) The experiment showed that 1.33 g of **X** contains 0.14 g of hydrogen and 0.63 g of carbon.

Calculate the empirical formula of **X**, using these data.

You **must** show your working.

**(3)**
parts.solution_md:
i) The** measurements** that should be made are:

- Mass / weight of each U-tube and their contents; **[1 mark] **
- Mass / weight before and after combustion / reaction; **[1 mark] **

ii) **Two** reasons why pure O<sub>2 </sub>(g), and **not** air, should be used are:

- To exclude water from the air; **[1 mark]**
- To exclude carbon dioxide from the air; **[1 mark]**
- For complete combustion;** [1 mark] **

iii) To calculate the empirical formula of **X**:

- Mass of oxygen Mass O = 1.33 - 0.14 - 0.63 = 0.56 (g); **[1 mark]**
- Moles of C, H and O | C | H | O |
|---|---|---|
| $\frac{0.63}{12}$= 0.0525 | $\frac{0.14}{1}$= 0.14 | $\frac{0.56}{16}$= 0.035 | ; **[1 mark]**
- Mole ratio and empirical formula | C | H | O |
|---|---|---|
| 1.5 | 4 | 1 |
| 3 | 8 | 2 | C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub>O<sub>2</sub>; **[1 mark] **

**Final answer:** **[Total: 8 marks] **

- *For part (i) you can also give*

  - *The mass of silica (gel) and soda lime *
  - *Initial mass and final mass or change in mass*
- *For part (ii)*

  - *Air will also contain water vapour and other gases such as carbon dioxide so pure oxygen will help the reaction go to completion *
- *For part (iii)*

  - *Make sure you show your working and show each stage of your calculation*
  - *If you make a mistake the examiner will be able to give you credit further on in the calculation if you make a mistake *

parts.problem_md:

The table shows some infrared absorption data.

| **Bond** | **Wavenumber range / cm**<sup>**–1**</sup> |
|---|---|
| C—H (alkane) | 2962–2853 |
| O—H (alcohols and phenols) | 3750–3200 |
| O—H (carboxylic acids) | 3300–2500 |
| C$=$C (alkene) | 1669–1645 |
| C $=$O (aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids) | 1740–1680 |

Explain how this spectrum shows that **Y** contains a carboxylic acid functional group, quoting data from the table.
parts.solution_md:
This spectrum shows that **Y** contains a carboxylic acid functional group as:

- (There is a broad) peak at 3220 cm<sup>−1</sup>
**AND**
(which indicates an) O-H (in a carboxylic acid);** [1 mark] **

**AND**
(indicates) C=O; **[1 mark] **

**Final answer:** **[Total: 2 marks] **

- *You can give any wavenumber or range of values within 3300-2500 and you can use OH or -OH for O-H*

parts.problem_md:
The mass spectrum of **Y** is shown.

![q2e-paper-3-jan-2022-edexcel-ial-chemistry](assets/026-q2e-paper-3-jan-2022-edexcel-ial-chemistry.png)

i) Show that the mass spectrum is consistent with **Y **having the molecular formula C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>4</sub>O<sub>3</sub> .

**(1)**

ii) Suggest the structure of the ion causing the peak at *m / z* = 43 in the mass spectrum of **Y**.

**(1)**
parts.solution_md:
i) The mass spectrum is consistent with **Y **having the molecular formula C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>4</sub>O<sub>3</sub> because:

- Molecular (ion) / M<sup>(+)</sup> peak at *m* / *z* = 88 
**AND **
(Relative molecular mass of) C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>4</sub>O<sub>3</sub> is 88; **[1 mark] **

ii) The structure of the ion causing the peak at *m / z* = 43 in the mass spectrum of **Y **is:

- CH<sub>3</sub>CO<sup>+</sup>;** [1 mark] **

**Final answer:** **[Total: 2 marks] **

- *The mass of C*<sub>*3*</sub>*H*<sub>*4*</sub>*O*<sub>*3*</sub>* is:*

  - *(3 x C) + (4 x H) + (3 x O) = (3 x 12) + (4 x 1) + (3 x 16) = 88*
- *You can also say the peak to the far right / with the highest **m** / **z** is 88 or give any indication of M*<sup>*(+)*</sup>* peak being 88 *
- *The charge on the ion can be in any place i.e. *<sup>*+*</sup>*CH*<sub>*3*</sub>*CO*
- *You can also give the formula CH*<sub>*2*</sub>*CHO*<sup>*+*</sup>* / CH*<sub>*2*</sub>*COH*<sup>*+*</sup>* / HC=CH(OH)*<sup>*+*</sup>* / CH*<sub>*2*</sub>*=C(OH)*<sup>*+*</sup>

parts.problem_md:
Compound **X** contains one type of functional group.

Compound **Y** contains two different functional groups.

Use the information in the question to deduce the structures of **X** and **Y**.

Compound **X**

Compound **Y**
parts.solution_md:
The structures of **X** and **Y **are:

- Structure of **X** 
CH<sub>3</sub>CH(OH)CH<sub>2</sub>OH; **[1 mark] **
- Structure of **Y** 
CH<sub>3</sub>COCOOH or CH<sub>2</sub>=C(OH)COOH; **[1 mark] **

**Final answer:** **[Total: 2 marks] **

- *You need to use the clues given in whole the question to help you answer this question *

  - *Compound **X** contains 1 type of functional group which must be an alcohol and has the empirical formula C*<sub>*3*</sub>*H*<sub>*8*</sub>*O*<sub>*2*</sub>
  - *Therefore there must be two -OH groups *
- *Compound **Y** has a molar mass of 88 g mol*<sup>*-1*</sup>* and contains both a COOH group and C=O group *

  - *COOH has a mass of 45 meaning a mass of 43 is left*
  
    - *-CH*<sub>*3*</sub>*CO and -CH*<sub>*2*</sub>*=C(OH) both have a mass of 43*
  - *This will involve a bit of trial and error when adding up the molar mass*
  - *Make sure the structure works, so each carbon atom has the correct number of bonds *

|---|---|---|---|

Geraniol has **two** different types of functional group.

Second functional group:

Brown / orange / yellow to colourless; **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
Phosgene can be formed from carbon monoxide and chlorine, using a catalyst of activated carbon.

CO (g) + Cl<sub>2 </sub>(g) ⇌ COCl<sub>2 </sub>(g)           Δ<sub>r</sub>*H* = –107.6 kJ mol<sup>–1</sup>

i) State and explain how the reaction conditions could be changed to maximise the **equilibrium **yield of phosgene in this reaction.

**(4)**

ii) The standard enthalpy change of formation for phosgene is Δ<sub>f</sub>*H* = –220.1 kJ mol<sup>–1</sup>.

Complete the Hess cycle and determine the standard enthalpy change of formation for carbon monoxide. Use the data from (b)(i).

Include state symbols in your cycle.

**(4)**

CO(g) + Cl<sub>2 </sub>(g) → COCl<sub>2 </sub>(g)
parts.solution_md:
i) The reaction conditions could be changed to maximise the **equilibrium **yield of phosgene in this reaction by:

Any **two** pairs from the three:

- Decrease the temperature; **[1 mark]**
- As the (forward) reaction is exothermic; **[1 mark]**
- Increase the pressure; **[1 mark]**
- As there fewer moles of (gas) on the product side; **[1 mark]**

EITHER

- Remove the phosgene (as it is formed); **[1 mark]**
- To reduce the concentration of product (so equilibrium moves to the right); **[1 mark]**

**OR**

- Add more CO / Cl<sub>2</sub>; **[1 mark]**
- To increase the concentration of the reactants (so equilibrium moves to the right); **[1 mark]**

ii) The completed Hess's law cycle:

![hesss-law-cycle-cocl2](assets/021-hesss-law-cycle-cocl2.png)

- Correct state symbols; **[1 mark]**
- Correct arrows; **[1 mark]**
- Calculation of value: Δ<sub>f</sub>*H* CO = −220.1 ‒ (−107.6)= −112.5 (kJ mol<sup>−1</sup>); **[1 mark]**

**[Total: 4 marks]**

- *Remember:** Changing pressure, temperature and concentration all affect the position of equilibrium so use the information in the question to determine what changes need to be made to shift the position of equilibrium to the right *
- *You are told the forward reaction is exothermic by the negative enthalpy change, Δ*<sub>*r*</sub>*H** = –107.6 kJ mol*<sup>*–1*</sup>* *
- *In a Hess cycle to calculate the enthalpy change of formation, the elements should be written underneath in the same quantities as they are found in the equation *

parts.problem_md:
The mass spectrum of a sample of phosgene is shown.

The peak at *m / z* = 65 has been omitted.

![q22c-paper-2-june-2021-edexcel-ial-chemistry](assets/022-q22c-paper-2-june-2021-edexcel-ial-chemistry.png)

i) Give the reason for the **ratio** of peak heights at *m / z* values of 102, 100 and 98

**(2)**

ii) Suggest an identity for the peak at *m / z* = 63.

**(1)**

iii) The peak at *m / z* = 65 has been omitted.

Draw **on the mass spectrum** the peak at *m / z* = 65, showing its relative intensity.

**(1)**
parts.solution_md:
i) The **ratio** of peak heights are at *m / z* values of 102, 100 and 98 because:

- Chlorine isotopes (35 and 37) are in the ratio of 3:1;** [1 mark]**
- (As there are) two chlorine atoms give the ratio of 9:6:1; ** [1 mark]**

ii) An  identity for the peak at *m / z* = 63 is:

- CO<sup>35</sup>Cl<sup>+</sup>; ** [1 mark]**

iii) The peak at *m / z* = 65, showing its relative intensity is:

- Peak drawn at 65 with relative intensity of 33.3; ** [1 mark]**

**[Total: 4 marks]**

- *For part i), the two marking points are marked independently meaning you can score marking point 2 without achieving marking point 1 *

  - *For marking point 1 you also score the mark by saying that 75% of chlorine exists as *<sup>*37*</sup>*Cl, and 25% exists as *<sup>*35*</sup>*Cl or show your workings:*
  
    - *CO*<sup>*37*</sup>*Cl*<sup>*37*</sup>*Cl*<sup>*(+)*</sup>* = 102*
    - *CO*<sup>*35*</sup>* Cl*<sup>*37*</sup>*Cl*<sup>*(+)*</sup>* = 100*
    - *CO*<sup>*35*</sup>* Cl*<sup>*35*</sup>* Cl*<sup>*(+) *</sup>*= 98*
  - *You should know that the ratio of peak heights for two chlorine atoms is 9:6:1*
- *To determine the identity for the peak at **m / z** = 63, take off the** M*<sub>*r*</sub>* for oxygen and carbon*

  - *63 - 12 - 16 = 35 so CO*<sup>*35*</sup>*Cl*<sup>*+*</sup>
  - *The + can be on any of the atoms*
- *The peak at **m / z** = 65 will be due to CO*<sup>*37*</sup>*Cl*<sup>*+*</sup>

  - *The peak will have a relative intensity of 33.3 due to existing in the ratio 3:1 with CO*<sup>*35*</sup>*Cl*<sup>*+*</sup>* (which has an abundance of 100)*

parts.problem_md:
In UV light, trichloromethane (CHCl<sub>3</sub>, boiling temperature 61 °C) reacts with oxygen to form phosgene and hydrogen chloride.

i) Write an equation for this reaction. State symbols are not required.

Give a reason for this.

Suggest whether an old bottle of trichloromethane can still be used for medical treatment, giving a reason for your answer.

parts.solution_md:

- 2CHCl<sub>3</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2COCl<sub>2</sub> + 2HCl; **[1 mark]**

ii) The rate of this reaction decreases with time because:

- Oxygen concentration will decrease; **[1 mark]**

iii) A precaution that should be taken when opening a bottle of trichloromethane is:

**[Total: 4 marks]**

- *You are given the formula for phosgene in part a) *
- *Multiples of the equation are accepted *
- *Other answers that will score the mark for part iii) include:*

  - *Use a well ventilated lab*
  - *Wear a gas mask *
- *For part (iv), you could have also gained a mark for stating that trichloromethane may have reacted (with oxygen) to give (toxic) phosgene / COCl*<sub>*2*</sub>

parts.problem_md: In a mass spectrum, the molecular ion is the ion which always has the
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is ****D**** because:**

- The molecular ion is formed when it is bombarded by a stream of electrons which causes an electron to be knocked off the molecule to form a positive ion
- The molecular ion is unstable so can fragment into smaller ions but compared to them the molecular ion has the greatest mass / charge ratio

**A** is incorrect as  the molecular ion does not always have the greatest abundance

  - [CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH]<sup>+</sup> → [CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>]<sup>+</sup> + CH<sub>2</sub>=OH
  - (3 x 12.0) + (7 x 1.0 = 43
- The structure of butan-2-ol does not allow for a peak due to C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>7</sub><sup>+</sup> due to the position of the -OH group

**A** is incorrect as  both would be expected to have this peak due to CH<sub>3</sub> <sup>+</sup>

**B** is incorrect as  both would be expected to have this peak due to C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub><sup>+</sup>

**D** is incorrect as  both would be expected to have this peak due to C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>9</sub><sup>+</sup>

parts.problem_md:
An aliphatic organic compound has the infrared spectrum shown.

![q14-paper-5-june-2021-edexcel-ial-chemistry](assets/009-q14-paper-5-june-2021-edexcel-ial-chemistry.png)

What are the bond stretches responsible for the peaks **P** and **Q** in the spectrum?

|   |   | **P** | **Q** |
|---|---|---|---|
| □ | **A** | O—H carboxylic acid | C`═`O carboxylic acid |
| □ | **B** | O—H carboxylic acid | C`═`O aldehyde |

parts.solution_md:

  - It also corresponds to the carboxylic acid O-H stretching vibration which occurs at 3300 -2500 cm<sup>-1</sup> but this would be a broad peak, so this can be ruled out
- The peak at **Q** occurs at approximately 1720 cm<sup>-1</sup>

  - This corresponds to the aldehyde C=O stretching vibration at 1740 - 1720 cm<sup>-1</sup>

**A** is incorrect as **P** is too sharp to be an OH stretch and Q is outside the region of 1725 - 1700 cm<sup>−1</sup> for a carboxylic acid C=O stretch

parts.problem_md: Which reagent produces a silver mirror when warmed with propanal but **not** when warmed with propanone?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is D**

- Tollens’ reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate) oxidises aldehydes to carboxylic acids, reducing Ag⁺ ions to metallic silver, which deposits as a silver mirror on the inside of the test tube
- Propanal (aldehyde) → silver mirror observed
- Propanone (ketone) cannot be easily oxidised under these conditions → no reaction

**A** is incorrect as 2,4-DNPH produces a **yellow or orange precipitate** with **both** aldehydes and ketones (it tests for the C=O group, not specifically for aldehydes), so it does not give a silver mirror

**B** is incorrect as acidified K<sub>2</sub>Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub> distinguishes aldehydes from ketones by an **orange → green** colour change, not a silver mirror

**C** is incorrect as Fehling’s solution distinguishes aldehydes from ketones by forming a **brick-red precipitate** of Cu<sub>2</sub>O, not a silver mirror

> **[exam-tip]**
> Silver mirror observation is **exclusive** to Tollens’ reagent. The three common tests for distinguishing aldehydes from ketones each give distinct observations:
> 
> - **Tollens’** → silver mirror
> - **Fehling’s / Benedict’s** → brick-red (Cu<sub>2</sub>O) precipitate
> - **Acidified K~2~Cr~2~O~7~** → orange to green colour change
> 
> All three require **warming** or **heating under reflux**; a Paper 4 examiner-report flag is candidates omitting the heat condition.

parts.problem_md:
A colourless liquid, **Z**, is known to be either ethanol (CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH) or methoxymethane (CH<sub>3</sub>OCH<sub>3</sub>).

The mass spectrum and infrared spectrum of **Z** are shown.

![Mass spectrum graph showing relative intensity versus m/z (mass-to-charge) ratio. Peaks at m/z 30, 40, 45, highest at 30.](assets/001-mass-spectrum-graph-showing-relative-intensity-v.png)

![IR spectrum of ethanol](assets/002-ir-spectrum-of-ethanol.png)

What is the relative molecular mass, *M*<sub>r</sub>, of compound **Z**?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C**

- The **molecular ion peak** (M<sup>+</sup>) in a mass spectrum corresponds to the mass of the whole intact molecule (less one electron, which has negligible mass)
- M<sup>+</sup> is always the peak at the **highest m/z**

  - Ignoring small isotope peaks at M+1, M+2
- M<sup>+</sup> = 46

  - So, *M*<sub>r</sub>(Z) = 46
- Both ethanol (CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH) and methoxymethane (CH<sub>3</sub>OCH<sub>3</sub>) have *M*<sub>r</sub> = 46, they are **structural isomers**, so the mass spectrum alone cannot distinguish them

**A** is incorrect as 30 is *M*<sub>r</sub> of methanal (HCHO)

**B** is incorrect as 44 is *M*<sub>r</sub> of CO<sub>2</sub>, propane, or ethanal (CH<sub>3</sub>CHO), not Z

**D** is incorrect as 60 is *M*<sub>r</sub> of propan-1-ol or ethanoic acid

> **[exam-tip]**
> The molecular ion peak (M<sup>+</sup>) is always the highest-m/z peak, NOT the tallest peak. The tallest peak is the base peak, which represents the most stable fragment; these are usually different peaks.
> 
> Ethanol (an alcohol, with C–O–H bonds) and methoxymethane (an ether, with C–O–C bonds) are structural isomers, identical *M*<sub>r</sub> but different functional groups, so IR is needed to tell them apart (see parts b and c).
> 
> When writing fragment ions, always include the positive charge: CH<sub>3</sub><sup>+</sup>, not CH<sub>3</sub> or CH<sub>3</sub>•. The mass spectrometer only detects positive ions, so every fragment ion must carry a + charge in your answer.

parts.problem_md: The broad IR absorption in the range 3230–3550 cm<sup>–1</sup> is characteristic of which bond?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is D**

- A broad absorption in the range 3230–3550 cm<sup>–¹</sup> is characteristic of the O–H bond of an alcohol
- Key IR absorption bands to memorise for paper 2:

  - O–H (alcohol): broad, 3230–3550 cm<sup>–¹</sup>
  - O–H (carboxylic acid): very broad, 2500–3300 cm<sup>–¹</sup> (extends below 3200; the distinguishing feature)
  - N–H (amine): sharp, 3300–3500 cm<sup>–¹</sup>
  - C=O: sharp, 1680–1750 cm<sup>–¹</sup>
  - C–H: 2850–3100 cm<sup>–¹</sup>
  - C=C: 1620–1680 cm<sup>–¹</sup>

**A** is incorrect as C=C absorbs near 1650 cm<sup>–¹</sup> (well below the stated range)

**B** is incorrect as C=O absorbs at 1680–1750 cm<sup>–¹</sup> (sharp), not 3230–3550 cm<sup>–¹</sup>

**C** is incorrect as C–H absorbs near 3000 cm<sup>–¹</sup> (medium width, lower in the range)

> **[exam-tip]**
> The IR absorption table is in the paper 2 data booklet. Use it, don't guess. Two key shape distinctions:
> 
> 1. O–H is broad
> 2. C=O is sharp
> 
> Watch for the alcohol-vs-carboxylic-acid O–H trap. These two peaks sit in different positions and have different breadths:
> 
> - Alcohol O–H: 3230–3550 cm<sup>–¹</sup> (broad)
> - Carboxylic acid O–H: 3300–2500 cm<sup>–¹</sup> (much broader, extending lower)
> 
> If a peak reaches down into 2500–2800 cm<sup>–¹</sup>, that's a carboxylic acid, not an alcohol.
> 
> For full marks in structured questions, you need to state **both** the specific bond (e.g. "O–H in an alcohol") **AND **the wavenumber range when justifying the presence of a functional group. Giving one without the other loses the mark.

parts.problem_md: What is the identity of compound **Z**?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is A**

- Both ethanol and methoxymethane have *M*<sub>r</sub> = 46

  - The mass spectrum alone does NOT distinguish them (they are structural isomers)
- Ethanol (CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH) has an O–H bond

  - This gives a broad absorption at 3200–3550 cm<sup>–¹</sup>
- Methoxymethane (CH<sub>3</sub>–O–CH<sub>3</sub>) is an ether with a C–O–C linkage but no O–H

  - It would show no absorption in the 3200–3550 cm<sup>–¹</sup> region
- The presence of the broad 3200–3550 cm<sup>–¹</sup> peak uniquely identifies **Z** as ethanol

**B **is incorrect as the absence of a peak near 1715 cm<sup>–¹</sup> (C=O stretch) does not discriminate. Neither ethanol nor methoxymethane contains C=O, so its absence rules out neither

**C** is incorrect as both compounds have *M*<sub>r</sub> = 46, so mass spectrometry alone cannot distinguish structural isomers

**D** is incorrect as methoxymethane is an ether (CH<sub>3</sub>–O–CH<sub>3</sub>) with no O–H bond. The broad 3200–3550 cm<sup>–¹</sup> absorption actually rules methoxymethane OUT, not in

> **[exam-tip]**
> When identifying a compound from combined mass spectra and infrared data, always cite the specific spectral evidence. Give the bond **AND **the wavenumber range.
> 
> For example, full-mark phrasing looks like: "the broad peak at 3200–3550 cm<sup>-1</sup> indicates an O–H bond in an alcohol".  The generic phrasing "because IR shows alcohol" loses marks in structured questions.
> 
> When two compounds are structural isomers (same *M*<sub>r</sub>, different connectivity), *M*<sub>r</sub> alone can't tell them apart.
> 
> The IR evidence is load-bearing. Before interpreting the IR, think about which functional groups each candidate compound actually contains:
> 
> - Alcohols → O–H (broad, 3200–3550 cm<sup>–¹</sup>)
> - Ethers → C–O–C (weak, 1000–1300 cm<sup>–¹</sup>)
> - Aldehydes / ketones / carboxylic acids → C=O (sharp, 1680–1750 cm<sup>–¹</sup>)

choices.label: A

choices.label: B
